Likelihood ratio test statistic

LRT.Rd

LRT() is a generic function for the likelihood ratio test statistic from a given object.

Usage

LRT(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'coxph'
LRT(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'coxme'
LRT(object, ..., type = c("integrated", "penalized"))

Arguments

object

any object from which a likelihood ratio test statistic, or a contribution to a likelihood ratio test statistic, can be extracted.

...

further arguments passed to or from other methods.

type

character, which of the two types of partial likelihood to extract, either "penalized" or "integrated".

Value

Returns the likelihood ratio statistic as a double.

Details

Currently implemented for "coxph" and "coxme" objects.

References

Terry Therneau, 2024: Mixed Effects Cox Models.

See also

coxph(), coxme(), logLik.coxme().

Examples

if (require("coxme", quietly = TRUE)) {
    efit1 <- coxph(Surv(y, uncens) ~ trt, eortc)
    efit2 <- coxme(Surv(y, uncens) ~ trt + (1|center), eortc)
    
    summary(efit1) |> print_lf()
    cat("LRT(efit1):", LRT(efit1), "\n\n")

    efit2 |> print_lf()
    list(LRT(efit2), LRT(efit2, type = "penalized"))
} else {
    message("R packages coxme and survival must both be installed to run example.")
}
#> R packages coxme and survival must both be installed to run example.
